title: fix: revert OpenAI image seed default (#16504)
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Reverts #16504 in full while we decide how image requests without a seed should behave.

- `/v1/images/generations` without a seed goes back to a random seed: a new image on every call, each one billed.
- Edits go back to picking a random seed at execution; identical unseeded edits still return the cached image.
- Also drops the `aspectRatio` passthrough on edits. It comes back with the seed decision.
- #16245 (FLUX.3) was meant to merge after #16504, so check it against this before merging.
- gen tests (`openai-image-cache`, `community-endpoints`), typecheck and Biome pass.

gist.headline: Fresh seeds, familiar edits
gist.blurb: Unseeded image generations get a fresh roll of the dice on every call. Identical unseeded edits keep their cached result; the edit-side aspectRatio passthrough is set aside while seed behavior gets sorted out.
gist.summary: Reverts the image seed default so /v1/images/generations uses a random seed for each unseeded call, identical unseeded edits still return the cached image, and edits no longer pass through aspectRatio.
gist.impact: Each unseeded generation produces a new, separately billed image, while repeating an identical unseeded edit returns its cached result.
gist.visual_concept: A garden of image frames represents unseeded generations: each seed grows a different picture. Beside it, a familiar framed edit sits in a small cache nook. Polli tends the garden with a tiny gardener's hat, emphasizing the contrast between fresh generations and repeatable edits.
